name: DNA double-helix model
summary: Watson and Crick proposed in 1953 that DNA is two antiparallel helical chains held by A–T and G–C base pairs, suggesting how genetic information is copied.
description: Watson and Crick proposed antiparallel helical chains with complementary A–T and G–C pairs, drawing on chemical constraints and others’ experimental work.
tier_reason: Complementary molecular structure supplied a reusable explanatory framework for replication, genetics and later molecular methods across generations.

impact.note: Explained how genes are copied, became common knowledge across many societies, and is the platform that molecular biology, biotechnology and genetic medicine stand on.

market.note: Commercial availability is not a milestone of a scientific knowledge result.

date.basis: Proposed structural model in the manuscript signed 2 April 1953; date belongs to model proposal, not discovery of DNA.

events.statement: Watson and Crick proposed antiparallel helical chains with complementary A–T and G–C pairs, drawing on chemical constraints and others’ experimental work.
events.caveats: The paper explicitly treats the model as unproved. Donohue, Franklin, Gosling, Wilkins, other King’s workers and prior chemical researchers are not collapsed into sole-person credit.

evidence.supports: Model, pairing, date and multiple contributions.
